title: It is finished (Luke 23:44–56)
hookLine: darkness, the veil torn, into thy hands, and a borrowed tomb

cards: A Catholic church on Good Friday afternoon looks wrong on purpose. The tabernacle stands open and empty. The altar is stripped bare: no cloth, no candles, no flowers.
There's no Mass; on this day and the next, the Church celebrates none. The priest walks in and lies face down on the floor, or kneels, in silence.
Then the Passion is read aloud, the whole story, and at one moment everyone in the church kneels, and nobody says a word for a while. Today is that moment, the way Luke tells it.

teach.b: It's about noon, and Luke says darkness covers the whole land until three. In the Douay-Rheims: "And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst."
The veil was the great curtain in the temple that hid the holiest place, where only the high priest went, once a year. Christians have read its tearing as the way to God being opened.
Then Jesus cries out with a loud voice: "Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit." Those words aren't new.
They're from a psalm of trust, Psalm thirty in the Douay-Rheims, and he dies praying it.

teach.h: IT IS CONSUMMATED: BROUGHT TO ITS END.
teach.b: Today's title comes from John's Gospel, where the Douay-Rheims renders it "It is consummated." In Greek it's one word, tetelestai: it is finished, brought to its end.
Two Gospels, two last words, and the Church keeps both. Then small, human things.

teach.h: A CENTURION, A TOMB, THE WOMEN.
teach.b: A Roman centurion who has watched it all says: "Indeed this was a just man." The crowds go home beating their breasts.

A council member named Joseph, from a town called Arimathea, who had not agreed with the others, asks Pilate for the body, wraps it in linen, and lays it in a tomb cut from rock where no one had ever been laid.
The women from Galilee follow to see where. They go home, prepare spices, and rest on the Sabbath, as the law asked.

teach.h: FATHER, INTO THY HANDS I COMMEND MY SPIRIT.
teach.b: And the Church's night prayer, at the end of every day, takes up his last words again: into your hands.

how: On Good Friday Catholics celebrate no Mass; they gather for the Passion, prayers, the veneration of the cross and communion from hosts consecrated the night before, and the Church's night prayer repeats the words into your hands.

practice: Today there's nothing to picture and nothing to do: just let it be quiet, the way the church goes quiet when everyone kneels, and let any thoughts go by.
If you pray, you can say his words once, at the start, and then nothing more: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

wordCard.voice: tetelestai. One Greek word on the cross: it has been finished, brought to its end, prayed with a psalm.

orig.note: Greek: it has been finished, brought to its end. one word in John 19:30.

carryVoice: Your line: into thy hands. In Luke, those are his last words. Sixty-six days now.
